claims.text: Sintered HfNbTaTiZr has a thermal conductivity of approximately 10–17 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ over 50–900 °C.
Lattice distortion and defects such as grain boundaries and dislocations impede electron and phonon propagation in HfNbTaTiZr and contribute to its low thermal conductivity.
The HfNbTaTiZr initial state is a random solid solution.
Annealing or other processing can induce chemical short-range order in HfNbTaTiZr.
Chemical short-range order in HfNbTaTiZr promotes HfTi and TiZr binary clusters and incipient B2-like structures.
Strong binary pair interactions can drive local ordering and phase formation.
Hf–Ti and Ti–Zr pair interactions drive ordering in HfNbTaTiZr without causing macroscopic phase separation.
The ordered HfTi and TiZr clusters form a percolating network in HfNbTaTiZr.
The ordered-cluster network locally regularizes the lattice parameter and reduces the RMS lattice-distortion amplitude.
Distortion relief from B2-like ordering reduces high-frequency phonon scattering more than the new cluster interfaces increase scattering.
Percolating ordered clusters provide low-resistance pathways for high-frequency phonons.
SRO can flatten a local energy landscape and reduce solute drag, as observed for edge-dislocation motion in MoNbTaW.
The dislocation-energy-landscape effect of SRO in MoNbTaW is analogous to a flattened phonon-transport landscape in HfNbTaTiZr.
SRO-induced distortion relief and percolation increase the lattice thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr above that of its random state.
Ordering shifts the high-frequency phonon DOS toward modes with higher group velocities.
A conductivity increase occurs only after the ordered-cluster network exceeds a percolation threshold.
Below the cluster-percolation threshold, HfNbTaTiZr retains the low-conductivity behavior of a random alloy.
At sufficiently extensive ordering, large brittle intermetallic precipitates can reverse the conductivity increase through interface scattering.
An annealed SRO sample should exhibit lower atomic displacement parameters, longer phonon lifetimes or lower scattering rates, and higher thermal conductivity than a quenched random-state control.
